name: Libreville
subtitle: Libreville, capital of Gabon: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 703,940 people lived in Libreville in the 2013 general census, concentrating nearly half of Gabon's national population.
Founded in 1849 by freed captives rescued from a slave ship, Libreville takes its name from this historic sanctuary of freedom.

parts.text: Libreville was founded in 1849 on the northern shore of the Gabon Estuary when the French naval vessel L'Élan intercepted the Brazilian slave ship Elizia and settled its liberated captives at a sanctuary town named Libreville ('free town').
Serving initially as the principal administrative base for French naval and exploratory expeditions in the Congo basin, it became the capital of the colony of Gabon in the early 20th century.
Following national independence in August 1960 under President Léon Mba, Libreville transformed from a modest port town into a major administrative and oil-industry coastal metropolis.
